<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914390_theRebbe_977" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914390_theRebbe_977__p007">
  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah reveals the three aspects of the repentance of Yom Kippur: the change in revealed soul powers, the drawing down of a new will from Ein Sof, and the essential bond of the soul's essence with the Awtsmoos.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is: "In sukkot you shall dwell... every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot... for I caused the children of Israel to dwell in sukkot..."</t>
    <t s="2">For "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot" and "for I caused [them] to dwell in sukkot" are two reasons for "in sukkot you shall dwell"</t>
    <t s="3">(as explained in the maamar of the continuum of Rosh Hashanah 5703,</t>
    <t s="4">cited above in section 2).</t>
    <t s="5">And the concept is,</t>
    <t s="6">that "in sukkot you shall dwell" is the revelation of the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="7">and in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="8">there are three matters.</t>
    <t s="9">The teshuvah itself,</t>
    <t s="10">and two matters in the root and cause of teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="11">For the teshuvah itself</t>
    <t s="12">(even the teshuvah of Yom Kippur)</t>
    <t s="13">is that a person changes himself,</t>
    <t s="14">that he leaves his previous existence and becomes a new existence.</t>
    <t s="15">For this change is in the revealed powers of the soul.</t>
    <t s="16">And this change in the revealed powers of the person is by his arousing and revealing the essence of the soul within him,</t>
    <t s="17">namely the essence of the soul that is related to the revealed powers.</t>
    <t s="18">[And similarly, regarding Above,</t>
    <t s="19">that the person becomes pleasing before Him as before the sin,</t>
    <t s="20">is</t>
    <t s="21">because through teshuvah a new will is drawn from Ein Sof, the Master of Will.]</t>
    <t s="22">And there is another matter in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="23">that is felt in it in revelation,</t>
    <t s="24">that the root and true cause of teshuvah is the bond of the essence of the soul</t>
    <t s="25">(which is above relation to the revealed powers)</t>
    <t s="26">with the Awtsmoos</t>
    <t s="27">(which is above the Master of Will).</t>
    <t s="28">Therefore,</t>
    <t s="29">also in the matter of "in sukkot you shall dwell"</t>
    <t s="30">(which is the revelation of the teshuvah of Yom Kippur),</t>
    <t s="31">there are three matters.</t>
    <t s="32">The matter of "in sukkot you shall dwell" itself – the change in the proximate encompassing [light],</t>
    <t s="33">that it becomes a settled light.</t>
    <t s="34">And the reason for this is – "for I caused [them] to dwell in sukkot" in the manner of an arousal from Above.</t>
    <t s="35">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="36">that it is similar to what was brought above in section 6, that this, that through an arousal from below the revealed will is aroused</t>
    <t s="37">(even though the arousal from below is incomparable relative to the will)</t>
    <t s="38">is not from the perspective of the revealed will itself</t>
    <t s="39">(for since the revealed will relates to worlds, it is defined by the fact that creations are incomparable relative to it and they cannot arouse it),</t>
    <t s="40">but rather because it is so determined in the absolute will.</t>
    <t s="41">And similarly, in the matter of "in sukkot you shall dwell",</t>
    <t s="42">the change, so to speak, that occurs in the proximate encompassing [light] to become a settled light is,</t>
    <t s="43">because "for I caused [them] to dwell in sukkot" in the manner of an arousal from Above,</t>
    <t s="44">a drawing from the Essence of Ein Sof, regarding which there is no distinction between encompassing and internal, and even the encompassing can come into settlement.</t>
    <t s="45">[Similar to how through teshuvah a will</t>
    <t s="46">(new)</t>
    <t s="47">is drawn from Ein Sof, the Master of Will.]</t>
    <t s="48">And there is another reason for "in sukkot you shall dwell" – "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot",</t>
    <t s="49">in the distant encompassing [light].</t>
    <t s="50">For the matter of dwelling</t>
    <t s="51">(settlement)</t>
    <t s="52">in the distant encompassing is not in the manner of an action</t>
    <t s="53">[for in the distant encompassing,</t>
    <t s="54">the level of "not a man",</t>
    <t s="55">action and change cannot apply,</t>
    <t s="56">as above in section 3],</t>
    <t s="57">but rather that "every native-born Jew"</t>
    <t s="58">"shall dwell in sukkot"</t>
    <t s="59">(the distant encompassing)</t>
    <t s="60">from their own side,</t>
    <t s="61">because they are rooted in the Awtsmoos.</t>
    <t s="62">[And this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="63">on the verse "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot": it teaches that all of Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah,</t>
    <t s="64">for at this level all of Israel are equal.]</t>
    <t s="65">And it is similar to the matter of the essence of Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="66">that from the perspective of the essential bond of the essence of the soul with the Awtsmoos, there is no defect from the outset.</t>
    <t s="67">And just as on Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="68">the matter of its essence shines in revelation also in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="69">that in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur it is felt</t>
    <t s="70">(as above)</t>
    <t s="71">that it is drawn from the essential bond of the essence of the soul with the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="72">so too is it in Sukkot,</t>
    <t s="73">that "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot" is a reason for "in sukkot you shall dwell",</t>
    <t s="74">that this, that the proximate encompassing is drawn into inwardness and becomes a settled light,</t>
    <t s="75">is felt in it,</t>
    <t s="76">that the reason for this is "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot",</t>
    <t s="77">in the distant encompassing,</t>
    <t s="78">the essential bond of the essence of the soul with the Awtsmoos.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
